text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Poland's new law on vetting collaborators or employees of secret services during communism goes into effect on August 3.
The National Radio and Television Council (KRRiT) meets on August 7 to choose a new supervisory board after Wednesday's meeting proved inconclusive.
Senate committees have added several dozen amendments to three bills on the reform of Poland's social security system.
Invest-Bank and Invest-Bank Holding SA, formerly Bank Staropolski, want to use capital links to increase joint market share in the car credit market to 10-14 percent.
Telecoms monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) will resign from part of its bill-collecting from those whose telephones did not work for more than three days due to flooding.

Farm bank BGZ made a 64-million-zloty pre-tax profit in June, putting its first-half pre-tax at 317.3 million, 35 percent better than in the same period last year. NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
